page: Microsoft Azure E128ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processors clocked up to 4.5 GHz, providing 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores using simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 1024.0 GB of RAM, adhering to an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture includes 7560 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. The instance lacks discrete hardware accelerators, maintaining a GPU count of zero.

Benchmark results place the compute and memory subsystems firmly within the top tier. The platform achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 232,766.23 and a PassMark CPU score of 131,808.85. Vector and cryptography processing capabilities are reinforced by native support for AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16) alongside SHA-NI and VAES, contributing to a PassMark extended instructions test score of 154,305.92. Memory throughput reaches 402.39 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB read blocks and 202.2 GB/sec for write operations.

Workload evaluation displays exceptional data processing scale, reaching 171.99 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, 40,176.82 on PassMark database operations, and 850.97 GB/sec on multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The system also handles CPU-based machine learning inference efficiently, generating 66.06 tokens per second on a medium 7B model. These metrics qualify the instance for massive in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise data warehousing, real-time analytics, and high-throughput memory-bound processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E128ads_v7 is a high-capacity memory-optimized instance powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at up to 4.5 GHz. Configured with 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores, the instance provides 1024.0 GB of RAM alongside 7560 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. It features advanced x86_64 vector instruction sets such as AVX-512 VNNI and BF16 while omitting discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across high-throughput scenarios, highlighted by 402.39 GB/sec large-block uncached memory read bandwidth, 171.99 million Redis SET operations per second, and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 232,766.23. The server offers strong qualitative resource density for massive transactional databases, in-memory caches, distributed big data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise computing.
